name: photosynthesis-entity-resolution-hard
description: An adversarial entity-resolution fixture containing multi-member synonym clusters, abbreviations, Unicode and punctuation variants, and high-similarity non-identity pairs. It evaluates retrieval recall, conservative semantic verification, transitive merge planning, deterministic canonical selection, and graph rewriting independently of Stage A extraction.

entities.name: CO₂
context: CO₂ is the inorganic carbon substrate attached to RuBP by RuBisCO.
Each fixed CO₂ molecule contributes one carbon atom to the Calvin cycle.

entities.name: carbon dioxide
context: Carbon dioxide is consumed as a molecular substrate during photosynthetic carbon fixation.
Carbon dioxide diffuses into leaves through stomata.

entities.name: CO2
context: CO2 is the ASCII rendering of the molecular formula CO₂.
The enzyme RuBisCO incorporates CO2 into an organic intermediate.

entities.name: G3P
context: In this graph, G3P denotes the three-carbon sugar glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate produced by the Calvin cycle.
Some G3P exits the cycle and contributes to carbohydrate synthesis.

entities.name: glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate
context: Glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate is a three-carbon sugar phosphate formed during the reduction phase.
Glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate is commonly abbreviated G3P.

entities.name: glyceraldehyde 3-P
context: Glyceraldehyde 3-P is a shortened spelling of glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate.
The Calvin cycle produces glyceraldehyde 3-P after reduction of 3-phosphoglycerate.

entities.name: Calvin cycle
context: The Calvin cycle fixes carbon in the chloroplast stroma using ATP and NADPH.
This source uses Calvin cycle for the photosynthetic light-independent reaction sequence.

entities.name: Calvin–Benson cycle
context: The Calvin–Benson cycle is the carbon-reduction cycle also called the Calvin cycle.
The cycle regenerates RuBP after producing G3P.

entities.name: light-independent reactions
context: In this source, light-independent reactions refers specifically to the Calvin cycle in the chloroplast stroma.
These reactions use ATP and NADPH generated by the light-dependent reactions.

entities.name: RuBisCO
context: RuBisCO catalyzes addition of carbon dioxide to RuBP during carbon fixation.
RuBisCO can also react with oxygen during photorespiration.

entities.name: ribulose-1,5-bisphosphate carboxylase/oxygenase
context: Ribulose-1,5-bisphosphate carboxylase/oxygenase is the full enzyme name abbreviated RuBisCO.
The enzyme has both carboxylase and oxygenase activities.

entities.name: ribulose bisphosphate carboxylase-oxygenase
context: Ribulose bisphosphate carboxylase-oxygenase is a punctuation variant of the full name of RuBisCO.
It catalyzes the initial carboxylation step of the Calvin cycle.

entities.name: RuBP
context: RuBP is the five-carbon carbon-dioxide acceptor used by RuBisCO.
RuBP is regenerated during the final phase of the Calvin cycle.

entities.name: ribulose-1,5-bisphosphate
context: Ribulose-1,5-bisphosphate is the five-carbon compound abbreviated RuBP.
RuBisCO attaches carbon dioxide to ribulose-1,5-bisphosphate.

entities.name: NADPH
context: NADPH donates reducing electrons during the reduction phase of the Calvin cycle.
NADPH is the reduced form of NADP⁺.

entities.name: reduced nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate
context: Reduced nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate is abbreviated NADPH.
This reduced electron carrier supplies reducing power to the Calvin cycle.

entities.name: light-dependent reactions
context: The light-dependent reactions occur at thylakoid membranes and produce ATP and NADPH.
They use light energy and release oxygen from water.

entities.name: light reactions
context: Light reactions is the shorter name for the photosynthetic light-dependent reactions.
The light reactions supply ATP and NADPH to the Calvin cycle.

entities.name: carbon fixation
context: Carbon fixation is the process of incorporating inorganic carbon dioxide into organic molecules.
RuBisCO initiates carbon fixation in the Calvin cycle.

entities.name: CO₂ concentration
context: CO₂ concentration is a measured environmental condition that can limit photosynthetic rate.
Changing CO₂ concentration changes substrate availability but does not create a different name for CO₂.

entities.name: carbon dioxide uptake
context: Carbon dioxide uptake is the movement and acquisition process by which a leaf takes in carbon dioxide.
Uptake rate depends on stomatal conductance and carbon dioxide concentration.

entities.name: oxygen
context: Oxygen is released when water is split during the light-dependent reactions.
Oxygen competes with carbon dioxide at the RuBisCO active site.

entities.name: glycerol-3-phosphate
context: Here G3P means glycerol-3-phosphate, a glycerol backbone intermediate, not glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate.
Glycerol-3-phosphate participates in lipid metabolism rather than the Calvin-cycle sugar output described elsewhere.

entities.name: 3-phosphoglycerate
context: 3-Phosphoglycerate is a three-carbon acid produced after the unstable six-carbon fixation intermediate splits.
ATP and NADPH are used to convert 3-phosphoglycerate toward glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate.

entities.name: Calvin cycle rate
context: Calvin cycle rate is a measurement of how quickly carbon-reduction reactions proceed.
The rate may change without the Calvin cycle becoming a different process.

entities.name: RuBisCO activity
context: RuBisCO activity measures the catalytic performance of the RuBisCO enzyme.
Enzyme activity is a property or measurement, not the enzyme entity itself.

entities.name: RuBP concentration
context: RuBP concentration measures the amount of RuBP present in the chloroplast stroma.
It is a quantitative property of the RuBP pool.

entities.name: NADP⁺
context: NADP⁺ is the oxidized electron carrier reduced to NADPH during the light-dependent reactions.
NADP⁺ and NADPH are chemically related but distinct redox forms.

entities.name: NADPH concentration
context: NADPH concentration is a measurement of the cellular NADPH pool.
It can influence Calvin-cycle reduction without being the NADPH molecule itself.

entities.name: chloroplast
context: The chloroplast is the photosynthetic organelle containing thylakoids and surrounding stroma.
Both light-dependent and light-independent reactions occur within the chloroplast.

entities.name: chloroplast stroma
context: The chloroplast stroma is the fluid compartment surrounding the thylakoids inside a chloroplast.
The Calvin cycle occurs in the chloroplast stroma.

labeled_pairs.rationale: CO₂ is the molecular formula for carbon dioxide.
CO₂ and CO2 differ only by Unicode subscript formatting.
Carbon dioxide and CO2 name the same molecular compound.
The fixture context explicitly uses G3P as the abbreviation for glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate.
Glyceraldehyde 3-P is a shortened rendering of glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate, abbreviated G3P.
The full and shortened phosphate spellings refer to the same sugar phosphate.
Calvin–Benson cycle is an expanded name for the Calvin cycle.
This source explicitly uses light-independent reactions for the Calvin cycle.
Within this source scope both names identify the same carbon-reduction cycle.
RuBisCO is formed from the initials of the enzyme's full name.
The spelling variant names the RuBisCO enzyme without punctuation and locants.
Both long forms name ribulose bisphosphate carboxylase-oxygenase.
RuBP is the standard abbreviation for ribulose-1,5-bisphosphate.
NADPH abbreviates the reduced form of nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate.
Light reactions is the shorter name used for light-dependent reactions.
CO₂ is a compound, whereas carbon fixation is the process that incorporates it.
CO₂ concentration is a quantitative condition involving CO₂, not the molecular entity.
Carbon dioxide uptake is a transport process involving CO₂.
Carbon dioxide and oxygen are distinct molecular compounds despite sharing photosynthesis context.
The abbreviation G3P is ambiguous, but the fixture's G3P entity means glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate, not glycerol-3-phosphate.
Glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate and 3-phosphoglycerate are separate Calvin-cycle metabolites.
Calvin cycle rate is a measurement of the process, not the process itself.
The Calvin cycle and light-dependent reactions are coupled but distinct photosynthetic stages.
Carbon fixation is one process within the broader cyclic sequence, not another name for the entire Calvin cycle.
RuBisCO is an enzyme; RuBisCO activity is a measured property of that enzyme.
RuBisCO is an enzyme and RuBP is its five-carbon substrate.
RuBP concentration is a measurement of the RuBP pool, not the compound itself.
NADPH and NADP⁺ are related but chemically distinct reduced and oxidized redox forms.
NADPH concentration is a quantitative property, not the electron-carrier molecule.
The chloroplast is an organelle; its stroma is one internal compartment.
Light reactions and light-independent reactions are complementary but distinct stages.

evaluation_contract.candidate_recall: Every labeled same_entity pair should survive the loose embedding threshold and per-entity top-K limit.
evaluation_contract.false_positive_rate: Among labeled different_entity pairs, the fraction incorrectly resolved as same_entity.
evaluation_contract.unresolved_pairs: Labeled pairs for which the verifier returns uncertain, produces no decision, or is not proposed by retrieval when a merge is expected.
evaluation_contract.canonical_selection: The earliest member in graph entity order must survive as the canonical entity for each merge cluster.
evaluation_contract.transitive_merging: Three-member clusters must collapse into one entity without merging semantically adjacent hard negatives.
evaluation_contract.entity_count_after: Seven expected clusters remove eleven duplicate entities, leaving 20 entities.
evaluation_contract.merge_rule: Only same_entity verifier decisions may authorize merges; embedding similarity remains retrieval evidence only.
